package_info.package_versions: N/A (active on site for 5 months, no versioning)
package_info.why_malicious: The Magecart skimmer is a malicious JavaScript code injected into the First Aid Beauty e-commerce website, designed to steal credit card information from users during checkout. The code is heavily obfuscated and encrypted, specifically targets US-based Windows users, and exfiltrates sensitive payment data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This behavior is unequivocally malicious as it compromises user privacy and financial security.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in e-commerce checkout page (First Aid Beauty site)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Heavily obfuscated and encrypted JavaScript skimmer code
(function(){var _0xabc=...; /* obfuscated code */ ...})();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the checkout form, intercepts credit card and payment data entered by the user, encrypts it, and sends it to a remote attacker-controlled server via HTTP POST, resulting in theft of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data from users is a classic sign of a Magecart-style skimmer. The use of obfuscation and encryption further indicates an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal e-commerce JavaScript should only process payment data for legitimate transaction purposes and never send it to unknown third-party servers. This code exfiltrates sensitive data to an attacker.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may use JavaScript to collect and transmit payment data, but only to trusted, PCI-compliant endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Sends data to untrusted external domains

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout page of the First Aid Beauty website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in the browser of site visitors.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits the checkout page, the skimmer code executes, hooking into the payment form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Interception of payment data entered by the user.

attack_chain.action: The skimmer collects, encrypts, and exfiltrates the payment data to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of credit card and personal information.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into checkout/payment pages
JavaScript code hooking into form submission events
Unexpected network requests to untrusted or unknown domains during checkout
Encryption or encoding of form data before transmission
file_indicators: Inline or external JavaScript with high entropy/obfuscation
Unexpected script tags or modified JavaScript files in checkout page source
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with the legitimate business or payment processor
Exfiltration endpoints with no business relationship to the site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce checkout pages for injected or obfuscated JavaScript, especially scripts that hook into payment forms and send data to unknown domains. Use web application firewalls and content security policies to block unauthorized script execution and outbound requests. Regularly audit site JavaScript for unauthorized changes and monitor network traffic for suspicious exfiltration patterns.
